Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
28 September 2026 .
Brent $ 107.47 + 3.02 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-20) · AI-assisted
01 NBC News reports Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with no deal reached.

02 Multiple outlets report eight US Marines were injured in an Iranian missile strike on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, with The Media Line noting the attack occurred two weeks ago.

03 Brent stood at $107.47 as of 08:55 UTC, up 3.02% over 24 hours; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-20, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with IMF PortWatch recording 1 transit on 2026-09-20 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day, and 95 indexed events logged in the past 24 hours underscoring the pace of the crisis. Brent stood at $107.47 as of 08:55 UTC, up 3.02% over 24 hours, with WTI at $95.05. On the diplomatic front, NBC News and CBS News report that President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the strait; the development is not new to this run but no public White House statement has followed, and no deal is in place. The Wall Street Journal, citing a single unverified source, reports on the behind-the-scenes details of failed truce negotiations. Iran's threat to close both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb comes from a single unverified source, صوت الإمارات, and has not been independently carried in this feed. On the military side, The Media Line reports that eight US Marines were injured in an Iranian missile strike on a vessel in the strait, describing the attack as having occurred two weeks ago; TRT World, The Express Tribune, AzerNews, and samaa.tv carry related reports, with no major wire in this feed. Iran claims, per Mehr News and as also carried by heraldscotland.com and Malay Mail, that a second US REMUS 600 underwater drone was seized in the strait; the US military has not publicly responded to this claim. As of 08:49 UTC, 177 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, easing over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
